        (7,8)-(7,11), (7,11)-(7,16) [2 edges]

        It's a tree (specifically, a rectilinear minimum spanning tree or similar, or connected graph without cycles?)

        (13,8)-(13,12): dist = 12 - 10 = 2

        5: (9,8)-(13,8): len 2 -> ADD (col 8: 2,8 - 6,8 - 9,8 - 13,8 are all connected!)
        6: (2,3)-(2,8): len 3 -> ADD (connects 2,3)
        7: (13,3)-(13,8): len 3 -> wait, does it connect 13,3? Yes! -> ADD
        Wait, in output 2:
        Are both (2,3)-(2,8) and (13,3)-(13,8) present?
        Yes! Rows 2,3: cols 5,6,7 are 5.
        Rows 13,14: cols 5,6,7 are 5, AND cols 10,11 are 5!
        Row 6,7: cols 10,11 are 5!
        Col 8: rows 4,5 are 5; row 8 is 5 (wait, (9,8) is at row 9,10, so row 8 is 5? Wait, (6,8) is rows 6,7, so row 8 has len 1 (just row 8)). Wait, row 8 has 5,5 at col 8,9!
        Rows 11,12 have 5,5 at col 8,9.
        What about col 3? Not connected!
        What about col 12? Not connected!
        Edges used in Output 2:
        (6,8)-(9,8) [len 1]
        (6,8)-(6,12) [len 2]
        (13,8)-(13,12) [len 2]
        (2,8)-(6,8) [len 2]
        (9,8)-(13,8) [len 2]
        (2,3)-(2,8) [len 3]
        (13,3)-(13,8) [len 3]
        Total 7 edges for 8 vertices! Exactly MST!

        Example 3:
        Blocks:
        (1,1), (1,10)
        (4,4), (4,10)
        (8,6), (8,10)
        Vertical on col 10:
        (1,10)-(4,10): len 1
        (4,10)-(8,10): len 2
        Horizontal:
        (1,1)-(1,10): len 7
        (4,4)-(4,10): len 4
        (8,6)-(8,10): len 2
        MST selects:
        (1,10)-(4,10) [len 1]
        (8,6)-(8,10) [len 2]
        (4,10)-(8,10) [len 2]
        (4,4)-(4,10) [len 4]
        (1,1)-(1,10) [len 7]
